checks.message: alert (intensity): 526 km away; the FULL pick set rejects it (1.95 s vs 0.23 s). An alert computed from only the earliest picks can still land there — see below.
alert (magnitude): 657 km away; the FULL pick set rejects it (4.39 s vs 0.23 s). An alert computed from only the earliest picks can still land there — see below.

With the first 4 pick(s) the alert's hypocentre is as compatible with the data as the true one: an early-stage EEW solution could legitimately land there. Mislocation is explained by geometry; the failure is that nothing downstream caught it.

azimuthal gap 339°, nearest station 1284 km, stations lie toward bearing 230°. OUT-OF-NETWORK: distance along the back-azimuth trades off against origin time; relations calibrated on in-network events are being extrapolated.

No station lies within 700 km of the alert's magnitude hypocentre (nearest 1934 km). With the cutoff working, NO magnitude could have been computed and no warning issued. The published M can only have come from stations the cutoff should have excluded — the safeguard was not applied.

[relation-dependent] at 1929 km, eew_illustrative gives ∂M/∂R = 0.32 per 100 km of distance error. Every 100 km the hypocentre is pushed away adds that much to M; at 700 km the same relation gives 0.38/100 km.

[relation-dependent] eew_illustrative at the alert's magnitude hypocentre with no cutoff → M12.6 (alert said M9.9). Agreement or disagreement here says more about the relation's coefficients than about the event — supply the operational relation to test it.

magnitude computed at 56.620°N 164.130°E 140 km, intensity predicted from 48.200°N 153.400°E 140 km: 1183 km apart. A magnitude inflated by a far hypocentre was then applied to a near one — the errors compound.
M9.9 > Mw 9.5 (Chile 1960, largest instrumentally recorded). JMA introduced a seismologically plausible M ceiling after 2016-08-01; ask what its value is and whether it applies on this code path.
if the alert were right, the network would have recorded ≈10^3.3 = 1,901× the ground motion the real M6.9 event produces at the same stations (differential, eew_illustrative).
prediction from the alert's inputs minus observed intensity: median +4.7 units (observed max 0).
the same intensity model fed the correct M/location misses observed by -1.0 — the intensity stage is faithful; the fault is upstream in M/location.
All stations are beyond Si & Midorikawa's ~300 km calibration range; predictions are extrapolations.
no single station moves M by >0.5 or the location by >144 km (largest: WAKKANAI, 55 km).
all picks within ±2.0 s of the independent solution.
all picks within ±10 s of the P times predicted by the reference origin.

summary: Out-of-network event: location under-determined along the back-azimuth (relation-independent).
With only the first few picks, the alert's hypocentre fits as well as the true one (relation-independent).
Magnitude used stations beyond the 700 km safeguard (relation-independent).
Magnitude and intensity stages used different hypocentres (relation-independent).
Magnitude above any instrumentally recorded event — a plausibility ceiling should have stopped it.
Magnitude far from the reference event's (≥1 unit).
Intensity over-prediction follows from the M/location inputs; the intensity model itself behaves.
